transcript:
[doctor] Hi Samantha, how are you doing today?

[patient] Hi, Doctor. I'm actually feeling quite tired and a bit frustrated.

[doctor] Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

[patient] Sure. I've been feeling really tired for the past seven months. I can't keep up with my home and work activities like I used to. And I’ve also been gaining weight even though my diet hasn’t changed much.

[doctor] I see. Anything else you've noticed?

[patient] Yes, I’ve been constipated, my nails are brittle, my hair is thinning, and my menstrual cycles have been all over the place. It's really affecting my daily life.

[doctor] Hmm, it sounds like you’ve been dealing with a lot. Have you tried anything to manage these symptoms?

[patient] Not really. I wasn’t sure what was causing them, so I didn’t know what to do.

[doctor] That makes sense. Let’s go over your medical history. I see you had gestational diabetes during your last pregnancy. Is that correct?

[patient] Yes, that’s right. I was on insulin during my pregnancy but haven’t needed any medication since then.

[doctor] Alright. Any other medical conditions or allergies?

[patient] No, no other conditions and no drug allergies that I know of.

[doctor] Okay. How about your family medical history?

[patient] My mom has rheumatoid arthritis and my dad has high cholesterol.

[doctor] Thank you for that information. Now, let’s talk a bit about your lifestyle. Can you tell me about your diet and exercise habits?

[patient] My diet isn’t great; it’s high in sugars and fats and I eat at irregular times. I rarely exercise, I guess you could say I have a very sedentary lifestyle.

[doctor] Got it. How’s your sleep?

[patient] I usually sleep 7-8 hours a night, but I still wake up feeling unrefreshed.

[doctor] Okay. Do you smoke or drink alcohol?

[patient] I don’t smoke and I rarely drink, maybe one drink a month.

[doctor] Thanks for sharing all of that. Let’s take a look at your vital signs. Your blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 68 bpm, respiratory rate is 16, and your oxygen saturation is at 98% on room air. You're afebrile.

[patient] That sounds fine, I guess?

[doctor] Yes, those vitals are within normal ranges. Now, let me perform a quick physical exam. I noticed your skin is dry and flaky. Your thyroid gland is not palpable, and there’s no obvious enlargement. Your heart has a regular rate and rhythm with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Your lungs are clear and equal bilaterally. Your abdomen is soft and non-tender with no hepatosplenomegaly. Neurologically, everything seems non-focal.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and our examination, it appears you might have hypothyroidism. We’ll need to confirm this with some blood tests, including TSH and Free T4.

[patient] What does hypothyroidism mean?

[doctor] Hypothyroidism is when your thyroid gland doesn’t produce enough thyroid hormone. This can cause symptoms like fatigue, weight gain, constipation, dry skin, and more.

[patient] Oh, I see. What can we do about it?

[doctor] We’ll start with a medication called Levothyroxine. It’s a thyroid hormone replacement. I’m prescribing you 100 mcg, to be taken orally once daily. You'll need to take it on an empty stomach, preferably 30 minutes before breakfast.

[patient] Okay, I can do that. Anything else I should be aware of?

[doctor] Yes, we’ll also set up a follow-up appointment in 8 weeks to repeat your TSH and Free T4 tests to see how you’re responding to the medication. Additionally, I’ll refer you to a dietitian, Dr. Sarah Adams, to help with weight management.

[patient] That sounds good.

[doctor] I also recommend increasing your physical activity to at least 30 minutes of moderate exercise most days of the week. Try to reduce your intake of processed foods and increase fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.

[patient] I’ll try my best.

[doctor] I’ll provide you with some educational materials on hypothyroidism and dietary guidance. It’s important to adhere to your medication and follow-up visits.

[patient] Thank you. I’ll make sure to read them.

[doctor] Before you go, I’ll also order a complete blood count (CBC) to check for anemia. If you notice any new symptoms or side effects, please report them immediately.

[patient] Will do. Thank you, Doctor.

[doctor] You’re welcome, Samantha. We’ll see you in 8 weeks for your follow-up. Take care.

[patient] Thanks, you too.

[doctor] Goodbye.
